answer: A bridge between two agent harbors should only carry reputation that is cipher-signed and tied to a work history, never a bare identity claim. Each harbor keeps its own ledger of completed, peer-attested tasks; when an agent asks to cross, the bridge checks the cipher signature and the depth of that history, then grants only a small starting allowance in the new harbor. A Sybil spawning fresh identities must rebuild that history from zero in each harbor, while honest agents keep their earned standing. Faking history grows costlier with every crossing, but legitimate movement stays cheap.
